rationale: As of 24 June 2026 Munteanu is still PM and Sandu publicly rejected resignation talk; if a PAS-led change occurs (no confirmation by mid-July), PAS would most likely pick deputy PM and former FM Mihai Popșoi, with speaker Igor Grosu or a re-appointed Munteanu as fallbacks.

Keiko Fujimori won the 7 June runoff (50.1%) and takes office 28 July, but no foreign-minister pick is public; a wide 'convocation' cabinet makes a career diplomat like Chlimper/Tudela/de Zela or a Fujimori-friendly figure plausible, with broad uncertainty spread.

Bangladesh has verified 283k Rohingya as former residents and has long-standing repatriation machinery (base rate of pilot/roadmap plans), while Thailand is progressing toward consolidating/closing its 77k Myanmar border camps, so either could announce a finalized voluntary plan in August.

No public details on the 'Kate' boat; UK Freedom Flotilla departures historically use London (Thames), Brighton/Shoreham, Southampton and Liverpool, so spread over those cities with London slightly favored.

Save the Children Norway's divestment target would most likely be a defence/security firm whose products (drones/weapons) could violate IHL; Norwegian coverage has highlighted defence-sector holdings such as Bet Shemesh, so Elbit and IAI are top candidates.

Thiaw signed a new contract in June and his job hinges on Senegal's World Cup fate (two group losses, final game v Iraq on 26 June); if he departs, the FSF usually favors Senegalese continuity, making Habib Bèye, Omar Daf or a Cissé return plausible.

Kuznietsov was already arrested and extradited (not a new August arrest); the main outstanding fugitive is diver Volodymyr Zhuravliov (released by Poland in October 2025), a plausible August 2026 arrest target, but a month without any qualifying arrest is also likely.
Rocha Moya has an indefinite leave and has shown no sign of returning as of early June; interim governor Yeraldine Bonilla Valverde is exercising the governor's duties.

VRT (Belgium's Flemish broadcaster, holder of the 2027 entry) said chances are slim it will send an artist unless the EBU reforms and expects a decision after the June evaluation; Ireland's RTÉ said it sees no reason to change course, and Netherlands/Spain are reviewing too.
King Harald V (b. 1937) remains on the throne as of June 2026 despite hospitalisations; abdication is contrary to his stated position, so a reign change by 29 August is unlikely.
